title: How did I do? (Aside from butchering the pronounciation of “Amereke”)...
transcript: Ranking every song in the musical ragtime from worst to best. Except I'm skipping some of these more interstitial tracks from the original cast album. Not because they're bad by any means, it's just kinda hard to rank them against the other songs, and I don't feel like it. The rest of them I have divided up into A, B, C, and D tiers. So starting with D tier. These are songs that aren't outright bad. I get what they're doing in the show, but they do kind of bore me. So in last place I have what a game, followed by crime of the century, followed by Atlantic City, which was left off the recent album. And I'm fine with that. Moving on to C tier. These are songs that are actually totally solid. I think they're well written, they're important to the narrative. They just don't do a lot for me as musical numbers necessarily. So I have Coalhouse demands, followed by Buffalo Nickel Photoplay, Inc, Henry Ford, his name was Colehouse Walker, nothing like the city, look what you've done, success, and what kind of woman. In B tier, I have three songs that are all really lovely, really beautiful, but maybe don't have the gut punch impact of the A tier songs. I have A Shtetl Iz Amereke goodbye my love, and Sarah Brown Eyes. And yes, that means I have 13 songs in the A tier. These are all stunning, gorgeous, top tier A+ bangers. Some of the best in the musical theatre canon. So my lowest ranked song in the A tier is the night the Goldman spoke at Union Square, followed by the prologue. Maybe controversial placement. It is brilliant. Obviously it's in the A tier, but it is a lot of info dumping. Next I have Coalhouse's soliloquy. Underrated. Next I have back to before our children journey on. He wanted to say and make them hear you. In fifth place, gliding. This song is very dear to me. It absolutely breaks my heart every time. And fun fact, from the Broadway Flea Market. This was an opening night gift from the 2009 revival. It's a flip book of a girl on ice skates. Fourth place, the song that's going around on Theatre TikTok right now, and deservedly so: New music. In third place, till we reach that day. In second place, your daddy's son. And in first place, of course, wheels of a dream.
classificationReason: A song tier-ranking of the Ragtime score, referencing the original cast album and 'recent album.' No discussion of seeing the 2025 production, the staging, acting, or direction — it is score/musical commentary, not a production review.
